title: SAIQE evaluation artifact: instantiation and two-arm evaluation harness for Security-Integrated AI-driven Quality Engineering
description:
Complete evaluation artifact for the paper Security-Integrated AI-Driven Quality Engineering for Reliable, Compliant, and Trusted Digital Systems.

It instantiates the SAIQE framework as two delivery pipelines over the same application, the same database and the same tools, differing only in test-authoring source, admission gate, finding triage and evidence recording. Test-authoring effort is held equal at 70 tests per arm, and the metric set, the arms, the budget and the analysis plan were pre-registered before the first measurement run.

Contents: the pre-registration; the frozen register of 31 seeded defects across 11 modules; both authoring specifications; both test suites; the security-property rule set; the policy catalogue and gate rules; the full harness; and every raw result file underlying the reported figures. A checker in the repository verifies that each figure in the manuscript matches the raw output.

The system under test is a snapshot of FCCSMS, a PHP federal case- and citizen-service management application, included under sut/ and published with the permission of Agile1Tech. That snapshot is deliberately vulnerable and must not be deployed or pointed at real data: it carries 31 seeded defects, 17 of them security defects, placed as runtime switches so that both the correct and the defective code path are present in source at all times.

Headline result: seeded-defect detection rose from 35.5% to 96.8% (Cliff's delta = +0.87, p = 0.0039) and all fourteen security-defect escapes were closed, but substituting mutation score for code coverage as the test-admission gate produced no discrimination between the arms (delta = -0.02, p = 1.000). The security-property checklist carries the effect, not the gate.
